segments.narration: Eight people sealed themselves in and started suffocating slowly. Nobody could work out where the oxygen was going.
Biosphere 2 is three acres of sealed glass in Oracle, Arizona. The crew went in on the twenty-sixth of September, 1991.
Sixteen months in, oxygen had slid from 20.9 percent to 14.5. That is the air on a four-thousand-metre mountain, indoors.
The answer was the building. Carbon dioxide was reacting with bare concrete, turning into calcium carbonate and locking the oxygen into the walls.
They grew 83 percent of their food and still lost a sixth of their body weight. Meanwhile the cockroaches and ants did fine.
